studies.Population: Japanese adults aged 40-69 in the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study
studies.Ethnicity Basis: Population imputation: stated Asian country/population -> Asian
studies.Ethnicity Supporting Text: kidney cancer risk in Japanese adults
studies.Reference: Green tea and coffee consumption and risk of kidney cancer in Japanese adults.
studies.Authors: Chen Y, Abe SK, Inoue M, Yamaji T, Iwasaki M, Nomura S, Hashizume M, Tsugane S, Sawada N, JPHC Study Group
studies.comparison_type: More than five cups of green tea per day vs rarely consumed green tea (women)

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 102,463 participants aged 40-69 were followed during 1,916,421 person-years (mean follow-up period, 19 years). A total of 286 cases of kidney cancer (199 in men, 87 in women) were identified.

cases.excerpt: A total of 286 cases of kidney cancer (199 in men, 87 in women) were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: Among women who consumed more than five cups of green tea per day, a statistically significant decreased risk was shown with a HR of 0.45 (95% CI: 0.23-0.89), compared to women who rarely consumed green tea.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Among women who consumed more than five cups of green tea per day, a statistically significant decreased risk was shown with a HR of 0.45 (95% CI: 0.23-0.89), compared to women who rarely consumed green tea.
